title: Coordinate-adic estimates for division and generators of saturated blowup transforms
statement:
Let $L$ be a characteristic-zero field and $A=L[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Fix ordered orthant vertices $\alpha_i$, let $D=\bigcup_i(\alpha_i+\mathbf N^n)$, $d_i=|\alpha_i|$, and $\Delta_i=\{\beta:\alpha_i+\beta\notin\bigcup_{j<i}(\alpha_j+\mathbf N^n)\}$. Let $I\subset A$ be an ideal and $f_i\in I$ with order $d_i$. Suppose their initial homogeneous forms have unique homogeneous division with quotient supports $\Delta_i$ and remainder support outside $D$, in every degree, and every $f\in I$ has an expansion $f=\sum_iq_i(f)f_i$ with $\operatorname{supp}q_i(f)\subseteq\Delta_i$ (hence unique). Let $P=(X_j:j\in J)$ be a nonempty coordinate ideal, with $\operatorname{ord}_P(f_i)=d_i$. Here $\operatorname{ord}_P(h)=\sup\{v:h\in P^v\}$, with $\operatorname{ord}_P(0)=\infty$. For every nonzero $f\in I$, writing $v=\operatorname{ord}_P(f)$, one has
$$\operatorname{ord}_P(q_i(f))\ge v-d_i.$$
For $h\in J$ and scalars $\xi_j\in L$, $j\in J\setminus\{h\}$, consider the continuous substitution into $B=L[[X'_1,\ldots,X'_n]]$ given by $X_h=e=X'_h$, $X_j=e(\xi_j+X'_j)$ for $j\in J\setminus\{h\}$ and $X_j=X'_j$ for $j\notin J$. Write $\sigma^*$ for this homomorphism. Then all $f_i'=e^{-d_i}\sigma^*f_i$ belong to $B$ and
$$(\sigma^*I)B:e^\infty=(f_1',\ldots,f_s')B,$$
where $J_0:e^\infty=\{g\in B:\exists m\ge0,\ e^mg\in J_0\}$. Equivalently, the saturation is generated by the individual transforms $e^{-\operatorname{ord}_P(f)}\sigma^*f$ for nonzero $f\in I$, and already by the displayed finite family. The assertions include $I=0$ with the empty family and commute with extension of the coefficient field.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), 207--302, Lemma 7.22, formula (7.23) and Corollary 7.24, printed pp.269--270; the saturation interpretation is the scheme-theoretic chart convention in the item. Supporting route: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94. No Stacks tag states this formal division result.

proof.text:
Put $H_i=\operatorname{in}_{(X)}f_i$, and use $P$-degree for the sum of exponents indexed by $J$. Each $H_i$ has $P$-degree $d_i$, since $f_i\in P^{d_i}$ and has total order $d_i$. Fix $0\ne f\in I$, let $q_i=q_i(f)$, and put $a_i=\operatorname{ord}_P q_i$, ignoring zero quotients. There is at least one nonzero quotient. Set $a=\min_i(a_i+d_i)$. The degree-$a$ part in the $P$-filtration of $\sum q_if_i$ is
$$S=\sum_{a_i+d_i=a}\operatorname{in}_P(q_i)\operatorname{in}_P(f_i).$$
It is nonzero: otherwise, take $t$ minimal among the total orders $\operatorname{ord}_{(X)}(\operatorname{in}_Pq_i)+d_i$ in this finite sum. Its total-degree-$t$ part would be a nontrivial relation $\sum Q_iH_i=0$, where each $Q_i$ is supported in $\Delta_i$ and has degree $t-d_i$. This contradicts the assumed unique homogeneous division (linear independence of the indexed quotient family). Higher total terms of $\operatorname{in}_P(f_i)$ cannot contribute at $t$. Thus $\operatorname{ord}_P f=a$, so $a_i\ge v-d_i$. No assertion about support preservation under the blowup substitution is used.

proof.text:
Work first in $C=A[X_j/e:j\in J\setminus\{h\}]\subset A[1/e]$, with $e=X_h$. Every element of $C$ can be written $a/e^m$ with $a\in P^m$: put a finite polynomial in the ratios over a common denominator, using $e\in P$. Conversely write $a\in P^m$ as $a=\sum_{|\beta|=m}a_\beta\prod_{j\in J}X_j^{\beta_j}$, with $a_\beta\in A$ and the finite sum over multiindices on $J$. Then $a/e^m=\sum_{|\beta|=m}a_\beta\prod_{j\in J\setminus\{h\}}(X_j/e)^{\beta_j}\in C$, because $X_h/e=1$. In particular $F_i=f_i/e^{d_i}\in C$. To verify its regular image in $B$, a monomial $X^\gamma$ of $f_i$ has $p=\sum_{j\in J}\gamma_j\ge d_i$ and maps, after division by $e^{d_i}$, to
$$e^{p-d_i}\prod_{j\in J\setminus\{h\}}(\xi_j+X'_j)^{\gamma_j}\prod_{k\notin J}(X'_k)^{\gamma_k}.$$
This polynomial has order at least $|\gamma|-d_i$. Consequently an output coefficient of degree at most $N$ receives contributions only from the finitely many $\gamma$ with $|\gamma|\le N+d_i$. Summing the displayed polynomials defines $f_i'\in B$ and proves convergence for every choice of the scalars, including nonzero ones. Multiplication by $e^{d_i}$ recovers $\sigma^*f_i$, so it is the stated quotient.

proof.text:
Let $T=IC:e^\infty$ and $g\in T$. Write $g=a/e^m$ with $a\in P^m$. By saturation, $e^kg=\sum_\ell c_\ell b_\ell$ for some $k\ge0$, $c_\ell\in C$, $b_\ell\in I$. Multiplying by $e^{m-k}$ in $A[1/e]$ shows $a\in IA[1/e]$, so some $e^t a$ belongs to $I$. Set $f=e^ta$ and $M=m+t$; then $f\in I\cap P^M$ and $g=f/e^M$. Indeed write $a=\sum_\ell u_\ell b_\ell/e^{r_\ell}$ in $A[1/e]$, with $b_\ell\in I$, $u_\ell\in A$. For $t\ge\max_\ell r_\ell$, multiplication gives $e^ta=\sum_\ell e^{t-r_\ell}u_\ell b_\ell\in I$; this equality holds in $A$ since $A\to A[1/e]$ is injective by coefficient shifting. If $g\ne0$, set $v=\operatorname{ord}_P f\ge M$. Apply step 1 to the supported division of $f$. For every $i$, $q_i(f)/e^{M-d_i}$ lies in $C$: when $M\ge d_i$ use $q_i(f)\in P^{M-d_i}$ and step 2, and otherwise use multiplication by $e^{d_i-M}$. Hence
$$g=\sum_i\bigl(q_i(f)/e^{M-d_i}\bigr)F_i\in(F_1,\ldots,F_s)C.$$
The reverse inclusion follows from $e^{d_i}F_i=f_i\in IC$. Therefore $T=(F_i)C$. The case $g=0$ is immediate.

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak n\subset C$ be the ideal in [lem-trf-coordinate-ratio-chart-completion]. That node identifies $\varprojlim_m C/\mathfrak n^m$ with $B$, with its map from $C$ exactly the chart substitution, including $F_i\mapsto f_i'$. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and the whole field), so [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-noetherian] gives that $A$ is Noetherian; $C$ is generated over $A$ by finitely many ratios, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes $C$ Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat] its $\mathfrak n$-adic completion $B$ is flat over $C$. This is flatness over the ratio chart; flatness of the blowup map $A\to B$ is neither asserted nor needed.

source.place: Tag 0G8S (lemma-affine-blowup-quotient-description); Tag 00MB (lemma-completion-flat); elementary fraction calculations with coordinate-ideal powers.

proof.text: Multiplication by $e$ on $C/T$ is injective: if $eg\in T$, some $e^{m+1}g$ belongs to $IC$, whence $g\in T$. Apply [lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection] with $M=B$ (flat over $C$ by step 4), $N=P=C/T$, and this injective $C$-linear endomorphism. The cited map acts on $B\otimes_C(C/T)$. Identify that module with $B/TB$ by $b\otimes\bar c\mapsto bc\bmod TB$, with inverse $b\bmod TB\mapsto b\otimes\bar1$. This inverse is well defined: for $t\in T$, $bt\otimes\bar1=b\otimes\bar t=0$, and any element of $TB$ is a finite sum of such terms. Balancing gives $bc\otimes\bar1=b\otimes\bar c$, so the two composites are identities. The tensor endomorphism sends $b\otimes\bar c$ to $b\otimes\overline{ec}$, which corresponds to $ebc\bmod TB$. Thus multiplication by $e$ on $B/TB$ is injective. For $m=0$, $e^mb\in TB$ already means $b\in TB$; for $m+1$, injectivity first gives $e^mb\in TB$, and induction gives $b\in TB$. Hence $TB$ is $e$-saturated. Since $IB\subseteq TB$, this gives $(IB:e^\infty)\subseteq TB$. Conversely $T=(F_i)C$ by step 3 and $e^{d_i}f_i'=\sigma^*f_i\in IB$, so $TB=(f_i')B\subseteq IB:e^\infty$. Both inclusions establish the required equality.

proof.text: For every $0\ne f\in I$, put $v=\operatorname{ord}_P f$ and $r_i=\max(0,v-d_i)$. Step 1 gives $q_i(f)\in P^{r_i}$. Apply the monomial calculation of step 2 to $q_i(f)$ and $r_i$: it defines $u_i=e^{-r_i}\sigma^*q_i(f)\in B$, since an output jet through degree $N$ uses only input monomials through degree $N+r_i$. Put $c_i=e^{d_i-v+r_i}u_i\in B$; its exponent is nonnegative, equal to $0$ if $v\ge d_i$ and to $d_i-v$ otherwise. Applying the same calculation to $f\in P^v$ defines $f'=e^{-v}\sigma^*f\in B$. Now $e^v\sum_i c_if_i'=\sum_i\sigma^*q_i(f)\,\sigma^*f_i=\sigma^*f=e^vf'$. Multiplication by $e^v$ is injective in $B$ by coefficient shifting, so $f'=\sum_i c_if_i'\in(f_i')B$. Conversely, each $f_i'$ is one of these individual transforms since $\operatorname{ord}_P f_i=d_i$. Thus the ideal generated by all individual transforms equals the saturated ideal of step 5. The calculation permits unit transforms and arbitrary scalars $\xi_j$.

proof.text: For a coefficient-field extension $L\subseteq E$, use coefficientwise images and $I_E=I\,E[[X]]$. The supported expansions imply $I=(f_i)$, so $I_E=(f_i)E[[X]]$. Each degree's indexed homogeneous basis remains a basis over $E$. Apply [lem-trf-homogeneous-continuous-formal-division] over both fields. Its division is computed degree by degree: subtract the already determined lower-degree quotient terms, then express the remaining homogeneous term in the stated basis. Thus every output jet is obtained from finitely many input coefficients by the same invertible matrices over $L$, and coefficientwise extension commutes with division. Over $L$ the remainder of each $X^\beta f_i$ vanishes since it lies in $I$; it therefore vanishes over $E$. By $E$-linearity it vanishes on polynomial multiples of the $f_i$, and by continuity and truncating each multiplier it vanishes on every $\sum a_if_i\in I_E$, $a_i\in E[[X]]$. Hence the supported-expansion hypothesis holds for $I_E$. A field extension preserves nonzero coefficients, so all $d_i$ and $P$-orders of $f_i$ are unchanged. Steps 1--6 apply over $E$ for all $\xi_j\in E$. For scalars coming from $L$, chart substitution commutes with extension because every output coefficient involves finitely many input coefficients; division by a fixed power of $e$ shifts coefficients. Consequently the generator and saturation equalities commute as well. No identification with $E\otimes_L A$ is used.

proof.text: For $I=0$ and the empty family there is no nonzero $f$ to test. Both $C\subset A[1/e]$ and $B=L[[X']]$ have injective multiplication by $e$ (coefficient shifting), so saturation of the zero ideal is zero. All displayed generated ideals are zero. The same reasoning applies after every coefficient-field extension. If $n=0$ the required nonempty coordinate set $J$ does not exist, so there is no omitted chart case.
